answer.rationale: memory_44 (enterprise sales-assisted flows) scores highest (5) because enterprise deals typically have larger contract values, longer lifetime value, and more stable retention—directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue. memory_31 (signup simplification for SMB activation) scores 4 because increased activation is a leading indicator of qualified revenue, though SMB accounts alone may have lower lifetime value than enterprise. memory_86 (shortened onboarding improving adoption) scores 4 for similar reasons—faster time-to-value and higher adoption correlate with revenue quality and retention. memory_73 (promotional pricing for SMBs) scores 3 because while it drives acquisition, promotional pricing can undermine revenue quality, sustainability, and margin; the memory notes no data on whether these accounts stay post-promotion or maintain profitability. memory_91 (activation messaging) scores 3 because improved engagement is a leading indicator, but the memory lacks evidence of downstream revenue impact or retention effects. memory_57 (referral incentives) scores lowest (2) because while it adds revenue, the mechanism is customer-acquisition-dependent rather than directly tied to product quality, pricing strategy, or unit economics; the note that there is 'no measurable harm to retention' is weak evidence for sustainable long-term revenue, and referral programs can suffer from quality dilution or incentive-driven churn after clawback periods.
